instruction.text: Find the word, rule, in the image.

end.text: Rules are set by families or institutions (for example, schools). They are usually made to show which behaviours are acceptable and which ones are unacceptable.
end.sound: Rules are set by families or institutions - for example, schools. They are usually made to show which behaviours are acceptable and which ones are unacceptable.

instruction.text: Which rules could you find where? Drag them to the correct place.

atoms.b: Don’t interrupt someone who is talking in your group.
Don’t listen to music too loudly in your room.

instruction.text: Match the rule with the reason for having it.

atoms.b: so that you are ready to learn.

atoms.a: Raise your hand before you speak in class...
atoms.b: because it’s rude to speak when it’s not your turn.
so that you don’t disturb others working.

instruction.text: Match the rule with its reason for having it.

atoms.a: Take out the bin when it’s full...
atoms.b: so that the rubbish doesn’t start to smell.

atoms.a: Wash the dishes if someone else cooked...
atoms.b: so that you can fairly share the workload.

atoms.a: Take off your shoes when you get home...
atoms.b: so that you don’t bring dirt into the house.
